clue.text: I break into song before I drink in Italy

indicators.note: the song with its added letter comes before the second I
the first I breaks into the song, splitting it open

parts.note: a chant is a song or sung refrain

explanation.surface: A tipsy traveller bursts into song before ordering a drink in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break into' puts the first I inside CHANT; 'before' then places that ahead of the second I.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine made in Tuscany, so it is a drink you would have in Italy.

clue.text: Agree that many are playing well

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
a player on form is performing well

explanation.surface: Many people agree that the team is playing well.
explanation.walkthrough: C for 'many' is the Roman hundred, a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply or fall in line with others is to go along with them.

clue.text: Originally where the winner can be found

definitions.meaning: to begin with, at the start

definitions.text: where the winner can be found
definitions.meaning: read literally, the position of whoever came top

explanation.surface: The winner was at the front from the very start.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at the outset, and literally names the top position in a race.

clue.text: Unaffected by the fan I waved about

indicators.note: something waved about is moved this way and that, mixing these letters

explanation.surface: Someone stays unmoved by a fan being flapped around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waved about' rearranges FANI.
explanation.definitionFit: An unaffected person is natural and artless, which is naive.

clue.text: Unfeeling in a person

parts.note: a person is a human

explanation.surface: Describes someone as cold and callous.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'in a person' as where feelings live; it is really two plain pieces placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruel and callous behaviour lacks compassion, which is unfeeling.

clue.text: Trap as a result of a mining disaster?

definitions.meaning: a hidden danger or snare waiting to catch someone

definitions.text: a result of a mining disaster
definitions.meaning: read literally, a fall in a coal pit, the kind of collapse a mining accident brings

explanation.surface: A snare is likened to the aftermath of a colliery accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden danger is a snare, and literally a collapse in a coal shaft is a fall in a pit.

clue.text: Congratulate the girl on your knee

parts.note: to pat someone on the back is to congratulate them
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone praises the little girl sitting on their lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link here; the definition is the bone at 'your knee'.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap is the bone at the front of the leg joint.

clue.text: Pale colour of some great interest

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A soft shade turns out to be fascinating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' signals letters taken from inside 'great interest'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint is a light shade, a hue diluted with white.

clue.text: Is this how a footballer is born?

definitions.text: Is this how a footballer is born?

parts.words: Is this how a footballer is born?
parts.note: the stock phrase for lively and well, taken literally of a baby already using its feet

explanation.surface: Wonders whether football players arrive in the world booting the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means lively and in good health, and literally pictures a living, kicking newborn.

clue.text: Could it make the girl seasick?

definitions.text: Could it make the girl seasick?

parts.words: Could it make the girl seasick?
parts.note: the word for less heavy also names a flat-bottomed barge, a boat that might give someone sea-sickness

explanation.surface: Asks whether something might make a young woman queasy on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Making the girl less heavy hints at the comparative of 'light'; a boat is the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat barge unloading ships in harbour is a small vessel, and a boat can cause sea-sickness.

clue.text: Nevertheless failing to resist

definitions.meaning: an adverb meaning all the same or despite that
read as two words, not holding out against something

explanation.surface: Someone gives in to temptation all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means despite this, and split in two it says not holding out against.

clue.text: Frank has nothing to write

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A man called Frank has nothing to put down on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank and candid both describe speech that hides nothing.

clue.text: Fish had an unpleasant aroma

definitions.meaning: a small silvery food fish of the salmon family
past tense of the verb meaning to give off a bad odour, British spelling

explanation.surface: The catch had gone off and stank.
explanation.walkthrough: The British past tense of 'smell' ends in -T where Americans write -ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A small silvery sea fish has this name, and it is also the British past tense of stinking.

clue.text: Measures our extremities

definitions.meaning: units of length of twelve inches each
the parts at the ends of our legs

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up their own hands and toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial units of length share the name of the body parts we stand on.

clue.text: Place to sit or stand in the market

definitions.meaning: a seat in a church choir or in the front of a theatre
a trader's booth or table at a market

explanation.surface: Somewhere at the market where you can either sit down or stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir or theatre seat and a trader's booth at a market share the name.

clue.text: Scope, a doctor goes over it

indicators.note: in a down clue going over means sitting above the next piece

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A physician reviews the extent of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes over' sets A and MB above IT in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Range or extent of influence is the bounds within which something operates.

clue.text: Slightly damp

parts.note: read 'damp' as a verb: to make a little wet, rather than an adjective describing something a little wet

explanation.surface: A description of something not quite soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damp' looks like an adjective, but here it is a verb: to wet lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: To wet something lightly is to dampen it a little.

clue.text: Social worker in real distress about no money initially being returned

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the reversed piece
distress puts the letters of the word real into disorder
distress puts the letters of the word real into disorder
being returned means the short piece is read backwards
initially takes the first letter of money

explanation.surface: A social worker is upset because no money is coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' gives ALER; 'initially' takes M, and 'being returned' reads the short piece backwards as MON, which 'about' wraps in the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a hospital official who handled patients' welfare, an early kind of social worker.

clue.text: Distraught lovers have the key to find the answer

indicators.note: distraught means upset and in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: E is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: Upset partners hold the key to sorting out their problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distraught' rearranges LOVERS into RESOLV; the musical key E finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out a problem is to solve or settle it, finding the answer.

clue.text: Solitary person about to get the clues solved

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

indicators.note: a puzzle solved is untangled, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A loner settles down to work through a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solved' gives CLUSE, the scrambled fodder, which follows the short word for about.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit lives alone, apart from society.

clue.text: Masseur misinterpreted the Dutch philosopher

indicators.note: misinterpreted means read wrongly, so the letters are taken in another order

explanation.surface: A masseur gets the Dutch thinker wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misinterpreted' rearranges MASSEUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance humanist scholar from Rotterdam is the best-known Dutch thinker of his age.

clue.text: Small creature that's game

definitions.meaning: a chirping insect related to the grasshopper
the bat-and-ball sport played in whites

explanation.surface: A tiny animal is described as up for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is the English bat-and-ball sport played with wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirping insect and the bat-and-ball sport share one name.

clue.text: Abandon the players who are not performing

parts.note: the cast are the actors in a play
an actor off stage is not performing

explanation.surface: Drop the actors who are not on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard something is to throw it away or desert it.

clue.text: Nearly having short drink out this evening

indicators.note: out here means on the outside, so the drink wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
nigh means nearly or almost

explanation.surface: Someone almost has a quick drink on a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' puts TOT outside NIGH; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The night of today is this evening.

clue.text: Head on one's shoulders

definitions.meaning: a headland, land jutting into the sea
a sleeveless cloak worn over the shoulders

explanation.surface: Echoes the saying about keeping a good head on your shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: A promontory is a headland, and a sleeveless cloak is a garment worn on the shoulders.

clue.text: The sound of animals' feet stop temporarily

indicators.note: the sound of says the answer is pronounced like the word the next words give

parts.note: paws are the feet of animals

explanation.surface: Padding animal feet fall silent for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sound of' signals a homophone: PAWS is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt briefly before carrying on is a short break in action.

clue.text: Bridge partners about to be in-eluded make a detailed examination

indicators.note: to be included says the piece is put inside the other

parts.note: South and North are partners at the bridge table
CA is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Card partners are drawn in to scrutinise something closely.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the four players are named by compass points and sit in partnerships, North with South and East with West.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrutinise something closely, line by line, is to examine it in detail.

clue.text: He is brought to account and it hurts

definitions.note: the definition is the verb in the clue's 'it hurts' sense, to give pain

explanation.surface: A man is made to answer for himself, and it is painful.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'it hurts' stands for 'it aches', so the verb carries the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To throb with a dull continuous pain is to be sore.

clue.text: Rush unhesitatingly causing worry

indicators.note: without hesitation means losing the hesitation sound er

parts.note: to career is to rush along headlong

explanation.surface: Rushing into things without pause causes anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhesitatingly' removes ER, the written form of a hesitant 'um'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxiety or concern is a burden on the mind.

clue.text: Not helpful at the hotel?

parts.note: the word for disobliging also reads as a hotel lacking rooms to put guests up in

explanation.surface: A grumpy hotel receptionist refuses to help.
explanation.definitionFit: Disobliging people refuse favours, and a full hotel cannot give rooms, lodging being accommodation.

clue.text: One by one sides lining up

definitions.meaning: a figure 1 set by another 1 makes 11
teams of eleven players, as in cricket or football

explanation.surface: Players file out individually as teams form.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket and football teams have eleven players, so a team is called an eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: Two ones side by side make the number eleven, and teams of that many players are called that.

clue.text: Goods for soldiers going into battle

indicators.note: going into puts the soldiers inside the battle word

parts.note: a battle is a fight
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Supplies are wanted for troops heading off to war.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are the army's sappers, a standard source of RE in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo carried by lorry, rail or ship is merchandise, or goods.
